tagline: Down the Jones Falls from a reservoir to Baltimore's mills.
intro: Falls Road starts in the north by Prettyboy Reservoir, near the hamlet of Alesia, and comes south through woods and rural country, past Butler and the country estates of the Green Spring Valley, into Baltimore. Below Cold Spring Lane it follows the Jones Falls, which once turned grist and cotton mills, and the valley's goods went to town on the Falls Road Turnpike.
Near the city line it passes Mount Washington, which some count as Baltimore's first suburb.

moments.title: Prettyboy Reservoir
moments.text: Baltimore's water backs up here behind a dam finished in 1932, and by tradition the reservoir is named for a settler's horse, Pretty Boy, that drowned in a nearby creek.

moments.title: Rockland
moments.text: At Old Court Road a small mill community of the early 1800s survives around a grist mill of at least 1810 that has made calico, wooden toys and artificial silk in its time.

moments.title: Bare Hills
moments.text: A free Black community from the 1800s, named for its mines, whose quarries supplied the stone for the mansion at Cylburn Arboretum.
